skills.name: compute_chow_class_of_incidence_condition
skills.description: Determines the class of a divisor representing a geometric incidence such as tangency in the Chow ring of a product of parameter spaces.
skills.preconditions: A smooth parameter space is given together with a geometric condition defined by a regular section of a vector bundle.
skills.postconditions: Produces the Chow class of the incidence divisor expressed in terms of the generators of the Chow ring.
skills.example: In the product P^2 × P^2, the class of pairs (p,ℓ) with p lying on ℓ is the product of the hyperplane class from the first factor and the hyperplane class from the second factor.

skills.name: apply_bezout_to_intersection_product
skills.description: Uses Bézout's theorem to compute the degree of the intersection of hypersurfaces given their classes in a projective space.
skills.preconditions: The intersection is proper and the varieties are defined by homogeneous equations of known degrees.
skills.postconditions: Returns the product of the degrees as the number of points counted with multiplicity.
skills.example: Two plane curves of degrees a and b intersect in a·b points counted with multiplicity.

skills.name: use_generic_finiteness_of_projection
skills.description: Shows that the projection from a closed subscheme to a factor is generically finite by checking dimension equality and dominance.
skills.preconditions: A closed subscheme of a product has expected codimension equal to the dimension of its fibers.
skills.postconditions: Establishes the existence of a dense open where the projection is finite.
skills.example: For the incidence correspondence of lines meeting a fixed line in P^3, the projection to the Grassmannian of lines is generically finite.

skills.name: compute_etale_monodromy_group
skills.description: Determines the monodromy group acting on the fibers of a finite étale map by analyzing how loops in the base permute the points.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale cover over a connected base is given.
skills.postconditions: Provides the permutation group describing the action on a generic fiber.
skills.example: The cover of the space of binary cubics by the set of their roots has full symmetric monodromy.

skills.name: derive_average_fiber_size_via_chebotarev
skills.description: Relates the average cardinality of fibers over finite fields to the proportion of elements fixing a point in the monodromy group using Chebotarev density.
skills.preconditions: A finite étale cover is defined over the integers and its monodromy group is known.
skills.postconditions: Gives the limiting average fiber size as the ratio of fixed‑point elements in the group.
skills.example: For a cover of some degree with full symmetric monodromy, the average number of rational points in fibers tends to one.

skills.name: apply_grothendieck_lefschetz_trace_formula
skills.description: Computes the number of rational points of a variety over a finite field by summing traces of Frobenius on étale cohomology.
skills.preconditions: The variety is separated of finite type over a finite field.
skills.postconditions: Expresses the point count in terms of cohomological data.
skills.example: For a smooth projective curve of genus g, the point count equals q+1 minus the sum of the Frobenius eigenvalues on the first cohomology.

skills.name: perform_deformation_to_transverse_configuration
skills.description: Replaces a given geometric configuration by a nearby one where conditions become transverse, preserving enumerative invariants.
skills.preconditions: The original configuration lies in a parameter space where generic members satisfy transversality.
skills.postconditions: Yields a configuration for which intersection numbers can be computed directly.
skills.example: Deforming a set of concurrent lines to a general position so that each pair meets in a distinct point.

skills.name: use_hilbert_scheme_of_curves_as_parameter_space
skills.description: Models families of curves of fixed degree and genus as points of a Hilbert scheme to apply scheme‑theoretic tools.
skills.preconditions: Curves are embedded in a projective space with a fixed Hilbert polynomial.
skills.postconditions: Provides a fine moduli space representing families of such curves.
skills.example: The Hilbert scheme of lines in P^3 is isomorphic to the Grassmannian Gr(1,3).

skills.name: apply_inclusion_exclusion_to_multiple_incidence_conditions
skills.description: Computes the class or count of objects satisfying several possibly overlapping conditions by alternating sums over intersections.
skills.preconditions: Each individual condition is represented by a class or count, and intersections of any subset are understood.
skills.postconditions: Produces the corrected total count avoiding over‑counting.
skills.example: Counting points lying on at least one of two lines in the plane by adding the counts on each line and subtracting the count on their intersection.

skills.name: evaluate_limit_of_rational_point_ratios_using_hasse_weil_estimates
skills.description: Shows that the ratio of point counts to the size of the base field approaches a constant by bounding error terms via Weil conjectures.
skills.preconditions: Families are defined over finite fields and have fixed dimensions and smooth fibers.
skills.postconditions: Guarantees convergence of the average to the expected value.
skills.example: For a family of smooth conics over a finite field, the number of rational points divided by the field size approaches one as the field grows.
